sections.heading: Artefacts & site of Rakhigarhi
sections.content: Prehistoric 5000 BCE In Haryana, pre Harrapan and Harrapan sites have been found. The major sites from where evidences of civilization are visible are Rakhigarhi, Banawali, Kunal, Agroha, Mittathal and Naurangabad. These sites have traces of paved roads, drainage system, a large rainwater collection and storage system, terracotta brick and statue production, and skilled metal working (in both bronze and precious metals) has been uncovered. sections.heading: Haryana- Monument- Kurukshetra
sections.content: Kurukshetra is a place of great historical and religious importance. It has a sacred association with the Vedas and the Vedic Culture. It was here that the battle of Mahabharata was fought and Lord Krishna preached his Philosophy of KARMA in the Bhagwad-Gita, to Arjuna at Jyotisar. In the very first verse of Bhagwad-Gita, Kurukshetra is described as DHARAMKSHETRA i.e Region of righteousness. According to Hindu mythology, the name Kurukshetra applied to a circuit of about 48 KOS or about 128 Km which includes a large number of holy places, temples and tanks connected with the ancient Indian traditions and the Mahabharat War and Kurus, the ancestor of Kauravs and Pandavs.

sections.heading: Pottery
sections.content: Potters and pottery making is an integral part of rural India and Haryana is no exception Potters are found in almost all the villages where they make utensils, decorative pieces and toys. Seasonal festivals are the times when the potters hundreds of toys like miniature cows, horses, people and houses.

sections.heading: Textiles-Weaving
sections.content: Haryana is very famous for its woven work, like shawls, durries and lungis. The durries from Haryana are embellished with spectacular geometric designs. The durries made with white triangles often set against a blue background is a popular pattern. Panipat is the centre for durrie making.

sections.heading: Haryana- Performing Arts- Music
sections.content: Haryana has a rich tradition of music. Even villages have been named after classical ragas. In Dadri tehsil, several villages are named on well known ragas such as Nandyam, Sarangpur, Bilawala, Brindabana, Todi, Asaveri, Jaishri, Malakoshna, Hindola, Bhairavi, Gopi Kalyana etc. Similarly in Jind district there are Jai Jai Vanti, Malavi etc.

sections.heading: Phalgun Dance
sections.content: During the month of February March, Phag Dance or Phalgun Dance is performed with joy and vigour. In this dance-men and women group together and involve themselves in a variety of movements, rhythm requiring sound co-ordination. The word Swang stands for disguise or imitation. It is performed in the old tradition on the open stage. It is an all male cultural troupe of twenty to thirty artistes, including the director, producer musicians and actors. The female roles are also played by males. A mutual dialogue between two characters or groups of characters; costumes and music are the main elements of the performance, accompanied by a number of folk instruments like Dholak, Nagara, Tasha, Been, Cymbals etc. Usually performed by villagers, swang is a blend of folklore, music and narration.

sections.heading: Haryana-Fairs & Festivals- Gugga Naumi
sections.content: The festival of Gugga Naumi in honor of a saint known as Gugga Pir is a festival, celebrated all over Haryana. In the lunar month of Bhadon (August-September) the devotees of Gugga Pir paint his image on the wall in turmeric and worship the snake. They also paint the image of snakes in black color. Milk and butter milk are poured into snake holes.

sections.heading: Artisans demonstrating at Surajkund mela
sections.content: Surajkund is famous for the crafts fair held in February every year. The fair brings together crafts persons including potters, embroiderers, weavers, wood carvers, metal workers, stone smiths, painters etc. from all over India. For entertainment there are performances by folk dancers, musicians, acrobats and magicians.
